items.text: Copper reacts with concentrated nitric acid to produce copper(ll) nitrate solution and nitrogen dioxide gas.

items.label: formula
items.text: C u ( s ) + 4 H N O _ { 3 } ( a q ) \rightarrow C u ( N O _ { 3 } ) _ { 2 } ( a q ) + 2 N O _ { 2 } ( g ) + 2 H _ { 2 } O ( 1 )

items.label: text
items.text: A student carried out an experiment to make some copper(Ill) nitrate crystals.

items.label: list_item
items.text: a The student started with 2.00 g of copper and added excess nitric acid. Calculate the maximum mass of copper(ll) nitrate, Cu(NO₃)₂, which could be obtained. (A: N = 14, O = 16, Cu = 63.5)

items.label: list_item
items.text: b Explain the method the student could use to obtain crystals of copper(Ill) nitrate from the copper nitrate solution. (ε)

items.label: list_item
items.text: The copper nitrate crystallises out of the solution as Cu(NO₃)·3H2O. The student did some calculations and worked out that he should make 7.61 g of crystals. He actually only made 5.23g. Calculate the percentage yield of the student's experiment.

items.text: Iron can be extracted from the iron(Ill) oxide produced, and the sulfur dioxide can be converted into sulfuric acid. In this question you can assume that the molar volume of any gas at rtp is 24 dm³.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Calculate the mass of iron(Ill) oxide that can be obtained from 480 kg of pure pyrite. (A: O = 16, S = 32, Fe = 56) (ε)

items.label: list_item

items.label: list_item
items.text: C The next stage of the manufacture of sulfuric acid is to convert the sulfur dioxide into sulfur trioxide (SO₃) by reacting it with oxygen.

items.label: list_item
items.text: i Write a balanced equation for this reaction. (2)

items.label: list_item
items.text: ii Calculate the volume of oxygen (measured at rtp) needed for the complete conversion of the sulfur dioxide produced in b into sulfur trioxide.

items.label: text
items.text: Strontium hydroxide, Sr(OH)₂, is only sparingly soluble in water at room temperature. In an experiment to measure its solubility, a student made a saturated solution of strontium hydroxide. She pipetted 25.0 cm³ of this solution into a conical flask, added a few drops of methyl orange indicator and then titrated it with 0.100 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid from a burette. She needed to add 32.8 cm³ of the acid to neutralise the strontium hydroxide.

items.label: formula
items.text: S r ( O H ) _ { 2 } ( a q ) + 2 H C l ( a q ) \rightarrow S r C l _ { 2 } ( a q ) + 2 H _ { 2 } O ( l )

items.label: list_item
items.text: a Explain what is meant by a saturated solution. (1)

items.label: list_item
items.text: b Calculate the number of moles of HCl in 32.8 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid. (1)

items.label: list_item
items.text: c Calculate the concentration of the strontium hydroxide in mol/dm³.
